in_greek.name: Παουλίνο
in_greek.long_meaning: Παουλίνο είναι ένα όνομα που προέρχεται από το λατινικό όνομα Παυλος (Paulus), που σημαίνει 'μικρός' ή 'ταπεινός'. Το όνομα Παυλος συνδέεται με τον Απόστολο Παύλο, έναν από τους πιο σημαντικούς ανθρώπους στη Καινή Διαθήκη. Το όνομα Παουλίνο είναι μια παραλλαγή του ονόματος Παυλος και χρησιμοποιείται ως προσωνύμιο για διάφορους ανθρώπους στον χριστιανικό κόσμο.

This cultural association later transformed in Christianity as St. Paulino became revered as a namesake representing humility and meekness.

historical_references.reference: Saint Paulinus of Nola was a 4th-century bishop and poet in what is now southern Italy. He was born in Nola and is known for his poetry and hymns in Latin, particularly his Carmina (Songs) and Epistles (Letters). Paulinus was a wealthy landowner and a Roman senator before converting to Christianity. He retired to Campania and became a hermit, later being ordained as a bishop. Paulinus played an important role in the spread of Christianity in southern Italy.

Paulino Alvarez was a Mexican Catholic priest and politician who served as the 38th President of Mexico from 1952 to 1958. Born in Atlixtac, Guerrero, he was educated in Puebla and became a priest in 1875. He was a political ally of Lázaro Cárdenas and was appointed as the Minister of Education during his presidency. Paulino Alvarez is known for his efforts to promote education and reduce poverty in Mexico.
